description: A spectacular double- or triple-height spiral staircase hall photographed at low camera height — approximately two to three feet off the floor — using a wide lens with a one-point perspective looking upward through the stairwell void. The staircase spirals continuously from ground to upper floors, its treads in dark oiled walnut, handrail in warm natural walnut with a live-edge quality, and slender dark steel balusters forming a regular vertical grid. The inner newel column is smooth plaster in warm off-white. Floor-to-ceiling multi-pane steel-framed windows at the far wall flood the space with brilliant cool-green daylight, revealing dense deciduous forest foliage beyond the glass. The hardwood floor at the base reflects warm amber light from above. A framed abstract blue-and-white artwork hangs on the left wall at upper mid-level, and the right wall shows a section of botanical-patterned wallpaper. Multiple warm glowing forms hang at varying heights through the stairwell void, their milky translucent surfaces radiating soft amber light that warms the plaster walls and walnut rail. Camera is pitched sharply upward, making the staircase spiral into the frame dramatically. The mood is dramatic and architectural.
